page.layout: Two coin medallions side by side at the top, each with a legend around the rim; below them one column of running text; a signature at the lower right of the text block.

main_text.p: TITVS Tribunus Maurorum, qui à Maximino inter priuatos relictus fuerat,invitus,atq; à militibus coactus, imperauit:atque intra paucos dies, post vindicatam defectione quam Magnus, vir consularis, Maximino parauerat,à suis militibus interemptus est. imperauit mēses 6.domi forisque fortunatus, sed Imperio parum felix. huic fuit vxor Calphurnia nomine, sancta & venerabilis fœmina,de genere Censorinorum, id est Pisonum. Hæc uniones Cleopatræ habuisse perhibetur,& lancem 100.librarum argenti, cuius plerique poëtæ meminerunt, in qua maiorum eius expressa visebatur historia.

CENSORINVS, vir plane militaris,atq; antsquæ[?] in curia autoritatis, cùm post omnes honores ( nam multis functus fuerat)in agro suo degeret senex ( atque uno pede claudicans, eo vulnere quod bello Persico Valeriani temporibus accepe-rat)factus est Imperator, & scurrarum ioco Claudius quasi claudicans appellatus est. Hic cùm se gravissimè gereret, neque à militibus ob disciplinam censoriam ferri posset, ab his ipsis à quibus Imperator fuerat designatus, interemptus est. extabat tempore Trebellij eius sepulchrum, in quo grandiusculis literis iuxta Bononiam incisi erant omnes eius honores, ultimo tamen versu adscripto.
Hactenus de iis qui Imperiū usurparūt à Gallieno ad Fla.Claudium:de quo mox tractabimus,persequentes ipsorū Rom. Imperatorum seriem.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions: left, a bearded head in profile facing right with a crown, legend "IMP" and "TITVS"; right, a laureate head facing right, legend "AVGVST. T. CENSORINVS". The legends are transcribed above as lines; the engraving itself is not text. "antsquæ[?]": the word is printed as "antsquæ" and does not read clearly as a Latin word; the printed form is kept. No catchword. No margin notes.
